title: City of Kings - Desecration Scenario - Let's Play - easy mode
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PgvLUj9yWDQ

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes his second run at City of Kings — after the botched story attempt — by dropping the campaign entirely and playing a single standalone: the Desecration scenario, on easy mode. He's candid that the game sits outside his wheelhouse; he's a narrative, dice-checking Ameritrash player at heart, and usually leaves euro-leaning designs like this to his game group. Easy mode bumps each hero to five starting health and each worker to two movement, and the difference is stark — in a game where "every minute change is huge," that cushion is the margin between floundering and winning. He works the loop cleanly this time: exploring for creature tiles, juggling workers across ore, wood, and fish, buying gear from shops, and climbing the skill trees toward needle claws and stone curse. Enemies teleport, track, reflect, and tempt his workers into traps, but he clears all five creatures — several before they can even activate — for his first outright win. He likens over-reliance on luck to Ghost Stories, where leaning on the dice means you're playing wrong. A satisfying close to the play sequence, and a clear-eyed admission that the win came with training wheels on.

----

Easy mode turned a losing game into a first win. Do you reach for lower difficulty to learn a heavy game, or insist on the intended challenge even if it means losing your first few plays?
